case_title.quote: GURMAIL SINGH v. STATE OF PUNJAB
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.quote: the accused, eight in number were broguht to trial
number_of_accused.reason: Judgment states eight accused were brought to trial.

accused_gender.quote: The injury attributed to him on the person of Baljinder Singh
accused_gender.reason: Accused are referred to with male pronouns and male names throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age is stated for any accused; the '18 years' reference concerns Randhir Singh's case.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of accused is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of accused is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation of accused is not mentioned.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No previous criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: Baljinder Singh succumbed to his injuries
victim_gender.reason: Victim Baljinder Singh is male, referred to with male pronouns.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the accused were all of one family and they were annoyed with the members of the victim family
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment describes rival families in the same locality, not any familial relationship between accused and victim.

offence_category.quote: a case of common intention is made out
offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under s.302 with common intention.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC ss.302/149, 302, 324/149 and 323/149; no Arms Act provision is stated
statutory_provisions.reason: Value omits ss.149, 324 and 323 and cites an Arms Act section the judgment never mentions.

weapon.quote: Gurnam Singh and Gurmail Singh were both armed with small knives (kirch)
weapon.reason: Lathis and kirch knives are both stated as weapons.

evidence_type.quote: primary reliance on the evidence of Sohan Singh PW 5, Rajwinder Singh PW6, the injured eye witnesses
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness and medical evidence are supported; no recovery evidence is mentioned.

confession.reason: No confession is mentioned in the judgment.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: Accused were all of one family and they were annoyed
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Common intention, enmity, weapons and fatal vital-part injury are all supported.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating circumstances are noted for the convicted accused.

trial_court_outcome.quote: Gurnam Singh, Gurmail Singh, Gurcharan Singh and Sher Singh were convicted
trial_court_outcome.reason: Convictions and acquittals match the judgment's account of the trial court.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Affirmed the trial court's judgment (Crl. Appeal No. 609-DB of 1997)
high_court_outcome.quote: This judgment has been affirmed by the High Court
high_court_outcome.reason: The High Court affirmed the trial court's judgment; 'Not applicable' is wrong.

final_outcome.correct_value: Sher Singh acquitted; appeals of the other accused dismissed, convictions upheld
final_outcome.quote: We, accordingly, allow the appeal of Sher Singh. The appeals of the other accused are dismissed.
final_outcome.reason: 'Convicted' ignores that Sher Singh's appeal was allowed and he was acquitted.

offence_finally_established.quote: A case of common intention is, thus, spelt out.
offence_finally_established.reason: Murder with common intention was upheld as the established offence.

imprisonment_type.reason: The judgment does not state any sentence or imprisonment type.

imprisonment_years.reason: No term of imprisonment is mentioned anywhere in the judgment.

fine_rs.reason: No fine is mentioned, so null is appropriate.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Dispute arose because the complainant party allegedly teased Nindo, daughter of Sher Singh; Baljinder Singh, not a brother, died.
neutral_facts.quote: teach the complainant party a lesson for having teased Nindo
neutral_facts.reason: Summary wrongly says victim's son teased, calls the deceased the victim's brother, and says the victim's brother died.

offence_severity.reason: Punishment range is not discussed in the judgment.

attempt_completion.quote: which had led to the death of the deceased
attempt_completion.reason: The offence was completed with death of Baljinder Singh.

physical_harm.reason: Headnote confirms injuries to both, with BS succumbing.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Eight accused charged; three convictions finally upheld (Sher Singh acquitted)
number_of_offences.quote: The appeals of the other accused are dismissed.
number_of_offences.reason: Only three accused's convictions stand after Sher Singh was acquitted, not four.

financial_property_loss.reason: No financial or property loss is mentioned.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Court did not expressly find premeditation; it noted accused drank together, then came out armed and raised a lalkara
premeditation_planning.quote: the accused had been drinking together in the house of Parshottarn Singh and had thereafter come out
premeditation_planning.reason: Court noted armed lalkara but did not expressly find premeditation; the planning finding came from Arun Nivalaji More.

motive.quote: teach the complainant party a lesson for having teased Nindo
motive.reason: Enmity over teasing of Nindo is the stated motive.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the injury in the present case had been caused directly and deep into the stomach of the deceased, a very vital part
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Court accepted the stomach injury as vital and fatal within a short time.

witness_credibility.correct_value: Credibility not separately discussed by the Supreme Court; trial court relied on Sohan Singh, Rajwinder Singh and medical evidence
witness_credibility.quote: The prosecution placed primary reliance on the evidence of Sohan Singh PW 5, Rajwinder Singh PW6
witness_credibility.reason: Value attributes credibility reasoning to the Supreme Court, which does not discuss witness credibility.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Accused ran away from the spot after the women's counter-attack with brickbats
post_offence_conduct.quote: As a consequence of this counter attack the accused ran away from the spot.
post_offence_conduct.reason: Judgment states the accused fled the scene, so 'Not stated' is wrong.

trial_duration.correct_value: Offence: 25 March 1996; High Court judgment: 19.01.2007; trial court date not stated; Supreme Court: 20 April 2011
trial_duration.quote: From the Judgment & Order dated 19.01.2007 of the High Court
trial_duration.reason: 19.01.2007 is the High Court judgment date, not the trial judgment; the High Court date is wrongly marked not stated.

legal_representation.quote: P.N. Puri, Manu Sharma, Sanjay Jain, D.P. Singh, Avneet Toor, Kuldip Singh

investigation_status.correct_value: Investigation completed; accused brought to trial
investigation_status.quote: After investigation, the accused, eight in number were broguht to trial
investigation_status.reason: Trial completion is supported, but a charge sheet filing is not explicitly stated.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural irregularity is noted in the judgment.

appeal_history.quote: We, accordingly, allow the appeal of Sher Singh. The appeals of the other accused are dismissed.
appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court outcomes are accurately described.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: The State supported the trial court's judgment; no specific prosecution argument on the stomach injury is recorded
prosecution_argument.quote: The learned counsel for the State has, however, supported the judgment of the trial court.
prosecution_argument.reason: The stomach-injury reasoning is the Court's own; the judgment records no such prosecution argument.

defence_argument.quote: the injury attributed to him could have caused as a result of a scuffle during the incident and was not possible with a lathi
defence_argument.reason: Culpable homicide, s.34 and scuffle arguments are all recorded.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the question as to whether the injury had been caused with the intention to cause death would be a matter of objective satisfaction of the Court
legal_principle_applied.reason: Objective satisfaction principle is correctly stated.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1958 465
precedent_relied_upon.reason: All listed precedents appear in the judgment's reference list.

sentencing_rationale.reason: The judgment gives no sentencing rationale.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors are identified by the court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Injury to a vital part (stomach) causing death within a short time; lalkara threatening retribution
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: a very vital part, which had led to death within a short time
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court relied on aggravating features such as the vital-part injury and lalkara, so 'None' is wrong.

other_sentence_order.reason: No sentence order beyond the appeal disposal is stated.
